seo.metaTitle: PNG File Size Checker - How Big Is My Image, Free
seo.metaDescription: See how large an image is when encoded as PNG, in kilobytes. Free and local - the picture is encoded in your browser and never uploaded to a server.
seo.longDescription: PNG file size checker encodes the loaded image as a PNG and reports the size of the result in kilobytes. That number is the size of a fresh PNG encoding, not necessarily the file already on your disk: re-encoding can land smaller or larger depending on the encoder settings and the content. For the weight of the original file, look at its properties in your file manager. Everything happens in your browser, so the image never leaves your device.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Reports a fresh PNG encoding of the pixels — not necessarily your original file's size.
A quick verdict against any size limit before you export.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
The tool encodes it as PNG and shows the resulting size in KB.
Compare that with the size limit of the place you plan to upload it to.
If the number is too high, resize the image, reduce its colors or convert it to JPG before exporting.

faq.q: Is this the size of my original file?
faq.a: Not always. It is the size of the file produced by re-encoding the image as PNG in your browser, which can differ from the original: a different encoder or settings may compress it differently.

faq.q: Why is my PNG bigger after editing?
faq.a: Editing and saving a PNG usually produces a larger file than the original, because the image is decoded to pixels and encoded again, and an encoder does not know which pixels you did not touch. Cropping first usually keeps the result small.

faq.q: How do I make the file smaller?
faq.a: Resize it down, reduce the number of colors with the quantize tool, or save as JPG or WebP, which are lossy formats designed for exactly this. Transparent areas also cost bytes in PNG - flattening them onto a solid background can shrink a file a lot.

faq.q: Is the image uploaded to measure it?
faq.a: No. The encoding happens in your browser tab, so your file never travels to a server and is not stored anywhere.
